response.justification: The candidate is a highly experienced generalist software engineer (15+ years) with strong full-stack, distributed-systems, and low-latency backend work, but the role's core requirement — deep, current C++/STL expertise — is barely represented: roughly six months of C/C++ component work at National Instruments in 2014–2015 and a university thesis project. C++ does not even appear in the listed skills. There is also no evidence of industrial automation domain experience, IEC 62443/SDL secure development practices, MQTT or industrial protocols (Modbus, OPC UA, IEC 61850), or message-broker-based architecture at scale beyond a self-described event-driven side platform. The seniority, systems thinking, and mentoring/teaching track record are genuine strengths, but the technical fit against the primary stack is weak enough that this would be a substantial retraining bet rather than a hire against the spec.
strengths: 15+ years of broad engineering experience, including low-latency, high-throughput microservices (millions of req/s) with async I/O, fibers, and caching
Strong software craftsmanship and quality culture: TDD, pairing, CI/CD, authored test frameworks and assertion libraries, plus demonstrated mentoring via workshops and courses
Proven ownership and cross-functional adaptability — founded and maintains an open-source event-driven geo-data platform deployed on Kubernetes
concerns: Minimal and dated C++/STL experience (~6 months in 2014–2015); C++ absent from the stated skill set
No industrial automation, IoT, MQTT, or industrial protocol (Modbus, OPC UA, IEC 61850) exposure
No evidence of secure development lifecycle practice or IEC 62443 cybersecurity standards, and no Azure cloud experience (AWS only)

key_factors.factor: Industrial automation & security standards (IEC 62443, MQTT, SDL)
Senior-level distributed systems and engineering craftsmanship
